aggregation: As the TC0-A gate (TC0-GATE, 02 §14): any required row FAIL -> FAIL; else any BLOCKED -> BLOCKED; else any UNKNOWN -> UNKNOWN; else PASS. A defect killed on no program is FAIL; a crash is never a kill. An evaluator error or a check that does not report is UNKNOWN. Every row's reasons are reported whatever the aggregate. Optional rows never satisfy a required row.

rows.acceptance: Clean worktree at a committed HEAD; every later row binds to it. A dirty tree is UNKNOWN (evidence not source-bound).
The Shen/JIT executable and library directory the gate runs on resolve to the flake's shen-jit output. No nix or no such flake output: BLOCKED. Another executable: UNKNOWN.
node --test tests/tc0/*.test.mjs tests/tc1/*.test.mjs: no failures. Any skipped test is UNKNOWN.

TC0-A gate rows still pass: the TC0-A evaluator (harness/gate.shen, manifest spec/tc0/tc0-a-requirements.json) is run as a prerequisite in this run, on the same HEAD, and its verdict is this row's status. Its rows are not re-implemented here. No report, another schema or another HEAD: UNKNOWN. Its waivers are reported as waivers of this gate.

harness/tc1-strict-replay.shen: for every TC1 hand fixture, after agreement with the model and the handwritten expectations, a tape of the sandboxed implementation recorded against the model's trace replays exactly and is admitted; for every retained failure in fixtures/tc1/handler-retained-failures.json the defect-free tape is admitted and the tape with its defect diverges at exactly the retained epoch. The retained cases must include an original and a minimized failure for each defect of the discovery-reduction-replay rows, and the tapes must bind the catalog the evaluator pins. model: models/tc1/handler-machine.shen with models/tc0/i64.shen, run in-process by the Shen harness on the flake-pinned Shen/JIT
not_covered: Exhaustive exploration beyond grammar H (at most 7 nodes; one-operation effects with I64 operation types, no closures): the generated family G is sampled, not exhaustive. The reduction campaigns cover four of the six injected defects (dynamic_clause_environment and resume_returns_argument show their first difference only through later values, for which no discrepancy class is defined). Steps the step record does not tell apart (which of two frames at one node an AbandonFrame or UnwindFrame step discards) are one catalog transition each. Multi-shot resumption, runtime and durable effects, and any soundness proof of the typing or one-shot rules. Slice C1 (structured tasks and bounded channels) is covered only by the optional rows task-hand-fixtures, task-commuting-obligation, task-solo5-guest and task-loop-closure, which no claim and no required row relies on: its contract (spec/tc1/CONCURRENCY.md) is a draft whose provisional choices (section 13), including the durable-effects-with-tasks questions, the owner has not confirmed; exploration is exhaustive only over grammar G (2-3 tasks, one or two channels), generated programs and the Solo5 guest are samples, reduction covers four of the nine task defects, FIFO is not checkable against the model's own records, and the fixtures, machines, guest and harness share one author lineage. The optional row solo5-control-replay covers a stride sample of the pure-call and handler programs, not the whole families, and no claim relies on it. Durable effects (slice D1, spec/tc1/DURABLE.md) are covered only by the optional rows durable-hand-fixtures, durable-guest and durable-validator-differential, which no claim and no required row relies on: the contract is a draft whose owner choices (DURABLE.md section 12) are unconfirmed, the evidence is the 16 hand fixtures with no generated or exhaustive family and no reduction, strict replay of retained failures or transition catalog for the durable machine, capabilities are forgeable values, and the fixtures, both machines and the harness share one author lineage. The validator differential compares only against the validator before the D1 edit, on the existing corpora and six mutation kinds. The optional row typing-differential is bounded evidence that the Shen sequent rules of spec/tc1/TYPING.md, with their fixed derivation checker, derive what the JavaScript validator accepts: the claim is derivable under rule set R, with no soundness proof of R, no proof that the checker implements R, only single-point mutants and boundary probes for invalid programs, and only the entry input [int, 0]; no claim relies on it. The service accepted-job contract (spec/service/ACCEPTED_JOB.md) and its Fenrir handler are not part of slice TC1 and are not rows of this gate; spec/service/service-requirements.json is a separate proposed manifest for them.
